rules.recovers: nearby calls misread as far jumps, which would glue a neighbouring function into the caller
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits bl as a jump only when the target is beyond the range of `b`; the shortest far jump in five ROMs is 1,960 bytes
rules.summary: a bl closer than farJump.minDistance to its target (the far-jump idiom fails) is a call

rules.recovers: far tails of long functions split off as functions of their own
rules.restsOn: a callee is never inside its caller; agbcc places a function's code contiguously
rules.summary: a bl to an address below the caller's code end is a far jump inside the caller

rules.recovers: pools and tables that would be free bytes for the gap scan to misread as functions
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits a function's literal pool and switch tables right after its code, separated only by alignment
rules.summary: the extent is the code plus the pools and tables right after it; claim those pools and every table

rules.recovers: functions proposed inside another function's unreached branch arms or alignment padding
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run, so the few bytes inside it the walk never reached are still its own
rules.summary: a dense function's free bytes inside its extent are claimed as dead code

rules.recovers: the call graph below every accepted function
rules.restsOn: a bl (or a bx after mov lr, pc) that settles as a call enters a function
rules.summary: the targets of the calls of an accepted function are functions
